new_statements.quote: Stress occurs (1) obligatorily on the first syllable of most stems (for "stem," see 2.1), (2) on the syllable before a contour except in emphatic sentences and yes-no questions, and (3) on a lexically determined syllable of some polysyllabic loans. These are termed respectively stem-initial stress, precontour stress, and lexical stress. [p. 20] ... 1.7.2.1. Stem-initial stress. Stress occurs on the first syllable of each stem in an utterance, including monosyllabic stems, except that most particles (a stem class) are not stressed [p. 21] ... 1.7.2.2. Precontour stress. Sentences which lack precontour stress (stress on the last syllable before the final #-contour combination) are emphatic or are yes-no questions. Other sentences take precontour stress. [p. 21]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Every stem carries stress on its first syllable (word/stem level, weight-blind); particles are normally unstressed. Independently, the last syllable before an intonation contour (phrase-final position) takes 'precontour' stress, except in emphatic sentences and yes-no questions. Some polysyllabic Spanish loans keep the source-language stress as lexical stress in addition to stem-initial stress, and such stems then do not take precontour stress unless suffixed or cliticised.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described as such; Day 1973 sec. 1.3.2 writes 'one degree of nonweak stress'. A stem can carry both stem-initial and precontour stress (or stem-initial plus lexical stress, e.g. escalera 'ladder', StressTyp2 ˈescaˈlera).
new_statements.exceptions: Particles (a stem class) are unstressed unless they take precontour stress; 'a few, however, are lexically stressed'. Polysyllabic loans have lexical stress corresponding to the source language. Emphatic sentences and yes-no questions lack precontour stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Day explicitly separates a word/stem-level rule (stem-initial) from a phrase-level rule (precontour = last syllable before a contour). Craig 1978 restates the same split ('Stress occurs on the first syllable of a stem, and on the last syllable of a phrase'). The native-speaker normative grammar (Delgado Rojas et al. 2007 p. 51) describes 'palabras independientes' (words in isolation, i.e. citation forms = phrase-final) as accented on the last syllable, which is Day's precontour stress observed on isolated words; it contradicts fixed-initial only if read as a word-level rule. DiCanio & Bennett 2018 note the phrase-final prominence may be a boundary tone rather than word stress.
new_statements.identity_note: jaka1246 'Jakalteko, Western' is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for ISO 639-3 jai, retired 2009-01-16 (CR 2008-056) and merged into jac Popti'/Jakaltek because the name is a dialect-group name (Concepción Huista / San Antonio Huista varieties). It is the same language as Glottolog popt1235 (Jacalteco/Popti'), which is already a catalog unit (CATALOG units[143], source StressTyp2 lect 589 = Day 1973:20, currently flagged 'contested initial~final' against Delgado Rojas et al. 2007 p. 51). Day 1973 describes the Jacaltenango dialect; no source specific to the western towns was found.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2016. Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10): 469-514 (author postprint).
sources.note: Sec. 6.1 p. 495: phrasal conditioning in Mayan fixed-stress languages — Q'anjob'al phrase-medial words take initial stress, phrase-final words stress the last syllable; 'Similar patterns have been noted for... Popti' (Day 1973), Akatek (England 2001)'. Second-hand.

sources.citation: Delgado Rojas, Edna Patricia; José Aurelio Silvestre Sánchez; María Elizabeth Silvestre Díaz; Antonio Benicio Ross Montejo. 2007. Stz'ib'nheb'anil Ab'xub'al Popti' — Gramática Normativa Popti'. Guatemala: OKMA/ALMG, Cholsamaj. 301 pp. (Glottolog ref 117935.)
sources.note: Cap. 2 sec. 3 'Acento', p. 51: 'El Popti' es uno de los idiomas con acento fijo, las palabras independientes se acentúan en la última sílaba; es decir, posee un acento agudo... no existen palabras cuyo significado dependan de la acentuación.' Bold on the final syllable of every example (aWAL, inTAM, ahtZOQ', elQ'OM, chintxuMU; loans xhiLAH, kenYAH, peCH'AN). 'Palabras independientes' = words in isolation = Day's precontour (phrase-final) position; the two sources conflict only if this is read as word-level stress.

Bookkeeping entry: ISO jai retired 2009-01-16 (CR 2008-056) and merged into jac Popti' (= popt1235) because the name is a dialect(-group) name; no references of its own. Its single WORLD_TARGETS ref (Craig 1977 / Day 1973 conflated) is the popt1235 literature.
